    From distance to transport time.

    IDEALISED CALCULATION

    Assume smoke follows one straight airflow path at a constant speed. Change the inputs to see how long that journey takes. These inputs are independent of the cabin’s qualitative fan control.

    Smoke sourceSampling inlet

    t = L / u assumes steady, uniform advection along a connected path. It excludes mixing, diffusion, deposition, plume dynamics and sensor response. A ceiling detector may not lie on that path. No alarm threshold, detection probability or safe cabin condition is predicted.

    What matters most?

    Give each criterion a priority from 0 (ignore) to 5 (highest). All four start equally weighted.

    DRAFT RATINGS / YOUR PRIORITIES

      How the score is calculated

      Con = 0, moderate = 1, good = 2. Multiply each rating by its priority, add the results, then divide by twice the sum of priorities and multiply by 100. Detector-name colours are not an extra criterion. Equal scores share a rank; all-zero priorities produce no ranking.

      Scores combine the draft ratings using your selected priorities. They do not establish measured performance, suitability for a spacecraft, or detection probability. See the source checks below. The ratings remain unverified assessments. Power, lifetime and particle-size specifications require supporting evidence.

      Research behind the detectors.

      RESEARCH EVIDENCE
      01 / PARTICLES

      Smoke properties affect detection.

      Size, composition and concentration all affect the signal. Research from Smoke Aerosol Measurement ExperimentCharacterised smoke from spacecraft-relevant materials and compared detector responses. Its findings help explain why a detector may respond differently to different smoke sources.Read the research ↗ helps explain why one detector does not fit every source.

      02 / TRANSPORT

      Airflow and detector placement.

      Sensitivity is only one part of the problem. Smoke must reach the sampling point. Ventilation and the source location influence that path.

      NASA fire-protection brief ↗
      03 / LIMITATIONS

      Particles and gases.

      Particle detectors measure airborne aerosols, while gas monitors measure selected gaseous combustion products. These complementary signals provide different information about a developing fire.

      Combustion Product Monitor ↗
      A few useful definitions +
      Aerosol
      Solid particles or liquid droplets suspended in a gas. Smoke and dust can both be aerosols.
      Scattering
      Light redirected by particles. An optical smoke detector measures this light, not the glow of a flame.
      Pyrolysis
      Chemical decomposition caused by heating; it can occur before visible flaming.
      Transport delay
      The time for smoke to reach a sampling point, separate from the instrument’s response once it arrives.
      Calibration
      Relating an instrument’s signal to a known reference under specified conditions.
